title: Analytical Electron Microscopy Studies of Simulated Solar Wind Implantation into Lunar Soil Analogs
content: The surface of the Moon is subject to irradiation from solar wind ions, predominantly H+ and He+. Lunar soil grains exposed to the solar wind show a range of microstructural alteration features collectively referred to as space weathering that depend on the composition and crystal structure of the individual soil grains and the duration of the exposure [1]. Common space weathering features in Fe-bearing silicates include surface amorphization to depths of order 100 nm and formation of nanophase metallic Fe (npFe0) [2]. These features have been studied in samples returned from the Moon as part of the NASA Apollo Missions, and also in the recent years from Chang’E 5 and 6 Missions from the Chinese Space Agency. Recent scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) -electron energy loss spectra (EELS) studies of lunar soils show that implanted solar wind He concentrates in bubbles or vesicles in npFe0 in silicate glasses [3] and is retained in high concentrations in vesicles in ilmenite (FeTiO3) [4].
